chapter: Larry in Chicago and New York
title: Offers to join Durante in New York; Dixieland Band piano changes
summary: Harry's mother kept him home when Jimmy Durante and Frank Christian wanted him; he relates the ODJB's pianist changes up to Billy Jones in London.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: By the way, in the old days, did you travel much, any of the bands you were with, did they get out of New Orleans?

Well, when I was a kid, I was playing around with Lane at the time. It was Pansy Lane. Yeah, Pansy Lane. And Jimmy Durante wanted me to join his band in New York. And Pansy Lane did join him, and Jack Loycanna on trombone. And Arnold, the deacon, on piano. No, on bass, that's right. He played bass with Jimmy Durante and Lane played the cornet. But he wanted me to join him. And then later on, Frank Christian was in New York. He wrote me. He wanted me to join him. But my mother said, well, I've got two boys away now. Well, Larry was with the Dixon Band Band, and Eddie, he was in Chicago working with Emil Christian, and I think, Yellen Nunes. And she said, no, I don't want you to go away. Staying home. She's staying home. So, then Ed went with the Dixon Band Band for a couple of weeks, right after Regis died. But I don't know what happened. He probably got home sick. He came on back home, and they got a fellow by the name of Sidney Mansfield, who I understand is a movie director now, California. And he left the band, and they got Frankie Signy rallying for a while, and they got Russell Rousey.
He stayed with him. He stayed with him.
Then when they went to England, Russell had to come back to New York for some reason rather than that. They got a piano player by the name of Billy Jones. And he stayed with him until they left.
Did they get him in New York?
Oh, he was an English piano player.
Yeah, I understand. I think it was Larry told me before he died. He had a pub in London called Two Keys or Cross Keys or something like that. And he's still in London.
Yeah, I think people have written articles about him over in the English papers occasionally.
Well, he's one of the authorities on Dixon Land Jazz over there. Larry said he was a very good piano player.
